children: Shares of software supply chain platform JFrog

jumped 3.8% in the morning session after it extended the previous session's post-earnings surge as the company delivered third-quarter results that beat expectations and lifted its full-year outlook on accelerating cloud adoption.

In its earnings release, the company reported third-quarter revenue increased 31% year over year to $179.2 million, topping consensus estimates of $165.5 million, driven by a 60% jump in cloud revenue to $101.5 million. Non-GAAP earnings reached $0.32 per share, surpassing projections of $0.23, the company said. Chief Executive Shlomi Ben Haim stated on the earnings call that AI-generated code is multiplying software binaries that require trusted storage and security, helping expand customers generating over $1 million in annual recurring revenue by 58%.

In addition, investors stepped in to buy the dip following the previous week's post-election tech routThe rebound follows a steep slide late last week when Democratic midterm victories sparked fears of tighter legislative curbs on artificial-intelligence data centers and capital spending.

In coverage by Reuters, Wall Street brokerages including Morgan Stanley and UBS characterized that sell-off as overdone, contending that extreme regulatory roadblocks to data-center developments are unlikely to play out.Sector sentiment was further supported after JPMorgan upgraded SAP to overweight, with analyst Toby Ogg noting in research reported by CNBC that enterprise AI shifting from pilots to production favors established systems of record.
What is the market telling us

JFrog’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 46 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 3 days ago when the stock gained 31.8% on the news that the company delivered a “beat-and-raise” third quarter for 2026, topping Wall Street expectations across key operating metrics, including revenue, adjusted operating income, and earnings per share.

According to a company press release, JFrog reported that total revenue reached $179.2 million vs S&P analysts’ estimates of $165.9 million, representing a 31% increase year-over-year. Cloud revenue surged 60% compared to the previous year's period to $101.5 million, while its trailing four-quarter net dollar retention rate stood at 124%. Looking ahead, the company projected revenue guidance of $184 million at the midpoint for Q4 2026, above analyst estimates of $168.4 million.

Management also raised full year sales and earnings per share forecasts.During the earnings call, the company emphasized that the rising complexity of AI-generated artifacts and increasing cyber threats are leading to larger and longer-term commitments from clients.

JFrog is up 78.5% since the beginning of the year, and at $106.32 per share, it has set a new 52-week high. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of JFrog’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,751.
